Per ADR-0015 and SPEC-design-system:

1. `apps/web/src/styles/_theme.scss`:

That is --bg, --surface, --surface-2, --border, --border-strong, --text, --text-muted, --accent, --accent-strong, --accent-soft, --focus, --on-accent, --danger, --danger-soft, --success, --success-soft and --overlay.

   - The section 6 reduced-motion rule, written against `*, *::before, *::after` with animation-duration and transition-duration set to 0.001ms !important. Also set animation-iteration-count to 1 !important.

2. `apps/web/src/styles.scss`:
   - `@use 'styles/theme'`.
   - `body` paints `background: var(--bg); color: var(--text)`, uses the body font at 16px/1.5, and sets `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`.

   - Section 2 rules: elevation uses borders and surface steps only; no blur backdrops, no gradient fills, no hover transforms; interaction transitions are color-only at var(--motion-fast).

  <behavior>
    - set('dark') sets `data-theme="dark"` on documentElement and stores { key: 'theme', value: 'dark' } in prefs
    - After TestBed.resetTestingModule() and a fresh injector (the same fake IndexedDB), init() restores `data-theme="dark"` and theme() === 'dark'
    - set('system') removes the data-theme attribute and stores 'system'
    - A stored value outside {system, light, dark} (for example 'purple') makes init() fall back to 'system' with no attribute
    - init() with no stored value leaves theme() === 'system' and no attribute
  </behavior>
  <action>
Per DSGN-01 and SPEC-design-system 1.4:

1. `PrefsRepo` (providedIn root) wraps NativeIndexedDBService over the `prefs` store:
   - `get<T>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>`
   - `set<T>(key: string, value: T): Promise<void>`, stored as { key, value }

2. `ThemeService` (providedIn root):
   - Exports `type ThemeChoice = 'system' | 'light' | 'dark'`.
   - `theme = signal<ThemeChoice>('system')` is exposed read-only.
   - `init()` reads prefs 'theme', validates it against the three allowed values (anything else becomes 'system'), and applies it.
   - `set(choice)` applies the choice and persists it.
   - Applying 'system' removes the data-theme attribute from `inject(DOCUMENT).documentElement`; applying 'light' or 'dark' sets `data-theme` to that value.
   - No matchMedia listener: the CSS media query already tracks the OS while System is selected (RESEARCH "Don't Hand-Roll").

3. app.config.ts: add `provideAppInitializer(() => inject(ThemeService).init())`, so a stored override applies before the first render.

4. App header actions:
   - A 44 px ghost button labelled "Display options" with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` toggles a disclosure panel.
   - The panel holds a `<fieldset>` with `<legend>Theme</legend>` and three native radio inputs (System, Light, Dark), each with a `<label for>`, styled as a segmented control whose segments are at least 44 px tall.
   - Escape and a click outside close the panel.
   - Selecting a radio calls ThemeService.set.
   - Signals only: `computed` and `signal` in the component, ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, and `@if` for the panel.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>pnpm --filter @dossier/schema build && pnpm --filter web exec ng test --watch=false --include=src/app/services/theme.service.spec.ts</automated>
    <fails_when>non-zero exit, or "No tests found" in the output</fails_when>
    <human-check>At http://localhost:4200 with the OS in dark mode, the app is dark. Choose Light, reload, and it stays light. Choose System and it follows the OS again. Switch the OS to light with System selected and the app follows without a reload.</human-check>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>
    - The theme.service.spec.ts cases for every behavior bullet pass.
    - `rg -q 'provideAppInitializer' apps/web/src/app/app.config.ts` exits 0.
    - `rg -q 'matchMedia' apps/web/src/app/services/theme.service.ts` exits 1.
    - `rg -c 'type="radio"' apps/web/src/app/app.component.html` prints 3.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>The theme follows the OS by default, an explicit choice persists across reloads, and it applies before the first paint of the app.</done>

  <behavior>
    - show('Saved', { kind: 'success', durationMs: 50 }) sets current() and clears it by itself after about 50 ms; show(msg, { durationMs: 0 }) stays until dismiss()
    - A second show() while one is visible queues it; it appears after the first is dismissed or expires
    - With localStorage.setItem stubbed to throw, init() resolves, storageUnavailable() is true, and update/getByKey/getAll/delete round-trip a Character in memory keyed by the nested keyPath core.id
    - In memory mode, requestPersistence() resolves false and never calls navigator.storage.persist
    - With indexedDB.open stubbed so the request fails with a DOMException named QuotaExceededError, init() resolves in memory mode instead of rejecting
  </behavior>
  <action>
Per SPEC-frontend-architecture sections 4 and 8 and SPEC-design-system 4.12:

1. `SnackbarService` (providedIn root):
   - A signal queue with `current = signal<Toast | null>(null)`, where Toast is { id, message, kind: 'info' | 'success' | 'error', durationMs }.
   - Methods: `show(message, opts)` (default kind 'info', default 4000 ms, 0 means sticky), `showError`, `showSuccess`, `showInfo`, `dismiss()`.
   - The service owns the timeout and clears it on dismiss.

2. `SnackbarComponent` (selector `cd-snackbar`, OnPush):
   - Renders current() fixed at the bottom, 26 px, centered, per 4.12: --accent-strong fill, --on-accent text, radius-full, and the one permitted shadow.
   - Uses `role="status"` with aria-live polite, or `role="alert"` for the error kind.
   - A sticky toast shows a 44 px dismiss button labelled "Dismiss".
   - It enters with an opacity change plus a 12 px rise at --motion-base.
   - Mount `<cd-snackbar />` once in the app shell template.
